answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No. Do not add the missed Thursday miles or the last two miles of the long run back into next week. You started this week drained, and extra miles on top would add load without adding fitness. Next week is about 31.5 miles, a step up from 27, which keeps the build moving toward the race without a make-up block.

new.analysis:
## The week in one view
The week came in at 27 miles against about 36 planned. Most of the gap came from one skipped run and two sessions cut short, and heat, short sleep and high stress drove those cuts more than any loss of fitness.

| Week | Miles | Longest run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jul 27 – Aug 2 | 32 | 11 mi |
| Aug 3 – 9 | 35 | 12 mi |
| Aug 10 – 16 | 32 | 9 mi |
| Aug 17 – 23 | 24 | 10 mi |
| Aug 24 – 30 | 27 | 11 mi |

## Why the heat changed the work
The easy runs felt manageable but drifted up in heart rate, so Tuesday's 10:24/mi came in at 153 bpm. That pushed much of the week's time into zone 3, which is why the easy share read about 11 percent. The easy effort was there in intent; the heat moved the numbers, so next week's caps are set for hot conditions.

## What went wrong on the long run
Sunday's run was meant to stay under 150 bpm, but it averaged 156 and climbed to 161. Stopping twice for water tells me heat was the limit, not the plan. Keep the long run at 11 miles under the cap and carry water; distance can wait until the temperature drops.

## Why no make-up miles
Adding the missed Thursday or the cut miles back would stack load onto a week that already started drained. The marathon needs the long run to grow toward 2.5 to 3 hours, and that growth comes from absorbing weeks, not from catching up. This is why next week holds the long run at 11 miles and keeps the threshold work short.

## What comes next
Eight weeks out, the long run is still two hours, so the build has to keep growing it. A medium-long run on Thursday and marathon-pace segments come back once sleep and heat settle, probably the week of Sep 7. Until then the sessions stay simple so your legs and sleep can recover.
